primary_source.title: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites

performed_reading: Opened the official ACL landing page and actual primary PDF; directly inspected abstract and sections 1 through 4, including neighbor-query generation, random schema-respecting database sampling and greedy suite distillation. This record makes no full-paper-reading claim.
commonality: Both procedures use output differences between a reference SQL query and altered SQL queries to reveal semantic mistakes that one observed result can conceal. Mutation-based semantic discrimination is established prior work.
difference: Zhong et al. construct small suites of generated database instances to distinguish a gold query from its neighbors. This comparison holds five actual released databases and existing operator controls fixed, and compares two deterministic anchor-selection rules.
novelty_status: The experiment tests the resource-specific effect of witness filtering on recorded semantic discrimination. It does not establish a new general mutation-testing method or query-equivalence criterion.
other_sources_reading_scope: The existing semantic-witness protocol names SemBench and Bench-U. This agent did not independently inspect their primary texts in this task and makes no new claim about their exact designs or novelty differences.
registration_context: This follow-up was designed after the original witness protocol and original 162/200 outcomes were known. New hash-baseline SQL results remain unmeasured at protocol freeze.
